sections.h2: Why was Oconee County split off from Clarke County?
sections.html:
Residents of southwestern Clarke County wanted their own government after the Clarke seat moved from Watkinsville to Athens in 1872, and the General Assembly answered in 1875 by creating Oconee County, per Wikipedia. Watkinsville became the new seat. The name comes from a Muskogean people of central Georgia and from the river on part of the eastern border.

The county is compact: 186 square miles, 184 of them dry land, all inside the Upper Oconee River sub-basin and all in the Piedmont. Clarke lies north, Oglethorpe east, Greene southeast, Morgan south, and Walton and Barrow to the west. A piece of the Oconee National Forest falls within its lines.

Four towns appear on the local map: Bishop, Bogart, North High Shoals and Watkinsville. Elder, Farmington and Salem are unincorporated. Progressive Farmer magazine ranked Oconee the third-best rural county to live in during 2006. Outside Watkinsville, the sheriff's office handles policing, while the town runs its own police department, and the courts belong to the Western Circuit of the 10th Judicial District.

sections.h2: How big has Oconee County grown, and what does a home cost there?
sections.html:
The county went from 32,808 people in 2010 to 41,799 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate reads 44,893. Owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $461,600 for 2020-2024, and 81.3% of homes are lived in by their owners.

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $2,221, and the drive to work averages 24.7 minutes. Density is 226.7 people per square mile across 184.34 square miles of land. At the 2020 census, 14,360 households lived in 14,998 housing units, 4.3% of them vacant, and 43.2% of those households had children under 18. Median age was 39.7, and 54.1% of residents lived in rural territory. QuickFacts also lists 2,128 veterans, 94.5% of households with broadband and a 96.4% high school graduation rate among adults 25 and over.

sections.h2: How is Oconee County governed, and what is daily life like?
sections.html:
Four commissioners and a separately elected chairman, all picked countywide for staggered four-year terms, hold the budget, taxing and ordinance powers. The chairman is the chief executive and appoints staff with the commissioners' input.

The weekly Oconee Enterprise covers local news, and a radio facility on Tower Place in the northeast corner broadcasts four stations. Walkability is limited, and a multi-use trail network has been under discussion since 2017, so most errands mean a drive.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges serve Oconee County?
sections.html:
Public school students attend one of eleven district buildings: six elementary, three middle and two high schools, enrolling about 5,615 children with 361 full-time teachers. Three private schools sit inside the county line as well.

The University of North Georgia keeps a satellite campus near Watkinsville, and the College of Athens, a private Christian college, opened there in 2012. Oconee County belongs to the Athens-Clarke County metropolitan area, and Clarke County adjoins it on the north.

School zoning is a district decision, so ask the district which school an address feeds before you describe it to buyers.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Oconee County?
sections.html:
A bill and a valuation come from two different desks here. The Tax Commissioner is at 7635 Macon Highway in Watkinsville, mails go to Suite 300, and the doors open at 8:00 and shut at 4:30, Monday through Friday. Phone (706) 769-3917 or text (706) 765-7790, according to the tax office FAQ.

  • Tax Assessors, (706) 769-3921: values, returns, exemptions
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: each adopts a mill rate
  • Courthouse record center, 23 North Main Street, (706) 769-3940: copies of warranty deeds

The appraisal staff say nearly 70% of a tax bill funds schools and the rest funds county government. They also note that they handle value only; the tax amount follows from the millage the two boards set.

sections.h2: What are the Oconee County due date and late charges?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property tax normally falls due November 15 in Oconee County, and mobile home tax on April 1.

  • Interest: bank prime rate plus 3 points a year, divided by 12 and applied monthly, with the state announcing the year's rate on or after January 1
  • Penalty: 5% of principal every 120 days past due, topping out at 20%
  • Enforcement: an unpaid account lets the Tax Commissioner levy on the property
  • Payment plans: set up by phone once bills are mailed, with interest and penalties still running until the balance is paid

Interest moves every month, so an old figure may fall short by closing day; ask for the payoff in writing before the sale.

sections.h2: How does an Oconee County appeal or homestead filing work?
sections.html:
Look in the upper right corner of your assessment notice for the phrase last date to file a written appeal. That date sits 45 days past the notice date, and a letter or the county's appeal form will do, but an emailed or online filing will not.

Owners may go to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator. After that ruling, a written notice sent to the assessors carries the case to superior court. Remember that appraisal staff rule on value only, never on the size of the bill.

Homestead rests on owning and living in the house on January 1, with the application in hand before April 1. Valuation is frozen as of January 1, so a renovation or demolition during the year counts from the next January 1. Exemption amounts are available at (706) 769-3921.

sections.h2: What should an Oconee County seller sort out before closing?
sections.html:
January 1 fixes both ownership and condition, which means a house sold later in the year still has a tax bill to divide at closing. Settle that split in the contract.

  • Request a payoff from the Tax Commissioner and hand a copy to the closing agent
  • Pull a copy of the warranty deed at the courthouse when the legal description is needed
  • Check whether the parcel is in unincorporated Oconee County or inside Watkinsville, Bishop, Bogart or North High Shoals, since a town may bill its own tax
  • Wrap up any open appeal before closing so a pending value cannot stall a refund

State refund claims for tax assessed in error have a three-year clock from payment, per the Department of Revenue's county tax facts page.

faqs.q: Which date does Oconee County use as the normal property tax due date?
faqs.a: Real estate and business personal property are due November 15 and mobile homes April 1. Charges begin to accrue after the date.

faqs.q: What is the last day to appeal an Oconee County value?
faqs.a: It is printed on the notice itself, 45 days after the notice date. The appraisal office will not accept an appeal filed electronically.

faqs.q: Which boards set the millage rate in Oconee County?
faqs.a: Two bodies: the Board of Commissioners for county government and the Board of Education for schools. A mill means a dollar of tax per $1,000 of assessed value, with assessed value set at 40% of market value.

faqs.q: How much does Oconee County charge for late property tax?
faqs.a: Monthly interest at prime plus 3% a year, and then a 5% penalty at each 120-day mark until penalties total 20% of principal.

faqs.q: Which towns are in Oconee County?
faqs.a: Four: Bishop, Bogart, North High Shoals and Watkinsville, the seat. Elder, Farmington and Salem have no town government.
